parameter: number of bicliques k (the biclique-cover number = solution size)
citation: Fleischner, Mujuni, Paulusma, Szeider, 'Covering graphs with few complete bipartite subgraphs,' Theoretical Computer Science 410(21-23):2045-2053, 2009 (prelim. FSTTCS 2007, LNCS 4855): the Biclique Cover problem (cover every edge of G by at most k bicliques), parameterized by k, is fixed-parameter tractable.

parameter: number of rounds t (the broadcast time = objective/solution value); not named explicitly, canonical parameter
citation: Fomin, Fraigniaud, Golovach, 'Parameterized Complexity of Broadcasting in Graphs,' WG 2023 (LNCS 14093) / arXiv:2306.01536 (full version in Theoretical Computer Science, 2024): because n <= 2^t, their 3^n n^O(1) algorithm yields an FPT algorithm parameterized by the number of rounds t with double-exponential dependence 2^{2^{O(t)}}; the double-exponential dependence is essentially tight under ETH (see 'Double Exponential Lower Bound for Telephone Broadcast,' arXiv:2403.03501, 2024, building on a Papadimitriou-Yannakakis construction).

parameter: number of terminals
citation: Dreyfus & Wagner, 'The Steiner problem in graphs,' Networks 1:195-207, 1971 (the 3^k n^O(1) subset dynamic program, which applies to the rooted directed case); Guo, Niedermeier, Suchy, 'Parameterized Complexity of Arc-Weighted Directed Steiner Problems,' SIAM J. Discrete Mathematics 25(2):583-599, 2011: Directed Steiner Tree is FPT parameterized by the number of terminals (whereas Strongly Connected Steiner Subgraph and Directed Steiner Network are W[1]-hard for that parameter).

parameter: the domatic number d (target number of disjoint dominating sets = solution value)
citation: Garey & Johnson, 'Computers and Intractability: A Guide to the Theory of NP-Completeness,' W.H. Freeman, 1979, problem [GT3] Domatic Number: deciding whether the domatic number of a graph is at least 3 is NP-complete; hence the problem is NP-hard already for the fixed constant d=3.

parameter: number of bins k
citation: General (binary-encoded) Bin Packing is NP-hard already for k=2 bins because 2-bin packing is exactly the Partition problem (NP-complete; Karp 1972; Garey & Johnson 1979 [SP12]); 2D Bin Packing generalizes 1D (set all heights = 1), so it is NP-hard for the fixed constant k=2. Cf. Jansen, Kratsch, Marx, Schlotter, 'Bin packing with fixed number of bins revisited,' J. Comput. Syst. Sci. 79(1):39-49, 2013 (prelim. SWAT 2010), who additionally prove the unary variant is W[1]-hard parameterized by #bins.

parameter: k = burning number b(G) (target number of rounds / fire sources)
citation: Kobayashi & Otachi, 'Parameterized Complexity of Graph Burning', IPEC 2020 (LIPIcs vol. 180, art. 21); journal version Algorithmica 84(8):2379-2393 (2022): Graph Burning is W[2]-complete parameterized by the burning number k.

parameter: k = number of selected/scheduled jobs (solution size / objective)
citation: van Bevern, Mnich, Niedermeier, Weller, 'Interval scheduling and colorful independent sets', Journal of Scheduling 18(5):449-469 (2015) (prelim. ISAAC 2012, LNCS 7676): Job Interval Selection (Independent Set on strip graphs, generalized to 2-union graphs) is fixed-parameter tractable w.r.t. the parameter k = number of selected intervals/jobs.

parameter: k = number of centers/radius-r balls
citation: W[2]-hard via the standard reduction from Dominating Set, which is W[2]-complete (Downey & Fellows, 1995, SIAM J. Comput.); stated explicitly for k-center by Feldmann, 'Fixed-Parameter Approximations for k-Center Problems in Low Highway Dimension Graphs', ICALP 2015 / Algorithmica 81(3):1031-1052 (2019): k-center is W[2]-hard for parameter k.

parameter: k = target number of vertices the tree must span
citation: Alon, Yuster & Zwick, 'Color-Coding', J. ACM 42(4):844-856, 1995: color-coding finds a minimum-weight k-vertex tree (treewidth-1 pattern) in 2^{O(k)} poly(n), giving FPT parameterized by the target size k; the weighted extension is standard (Cygan et al., Parameterized Algorithms). [Gate-4: the earlier Hassidim-Keller-Lewenstein-Roditty WADS 2013 secondary was min-weight k-PATH, not k-tree; dropped — AYZ carries the value alone.]

parameter: k = budget (number of sets selected)
citation: Bonnet, Paschos, Sikora, 'Parameterized exact and approximation algorithms for maximum k-set cover and related satisfiability problems', RAIRO-ITA 50(3):227-240 (2016): Max k-Set Cover (= Maximum Coverage) is W[2]-hard parameterized by k (the number of sets) and FPT parameterized by p (elements covered). Also folklore from Set Cover W[2]-completeness (Downey & Fellows, 1995).

parameter: p, the cardinality of the selected subset
citation: Cai, 'Parameterized Complexity of Cardinality Constrained Optimization Problems,' The Computer Journal 51(1):102-121, 2008 — Densest-k-Subgraph is W[1]-hard parameterized by k; metric max-sum p-dispersion equals Densest-p-Subgraph plus an additive constant under the standard {1,2}-metric (edge=2, non-edge=1), a parameter-preserving reduction with p=k (equivalently the classical Clique reduction, Clique being W[1]-complete, Downey & Fellows 1995).

parameter: treewidth
citation: K. Jansen, 'The optimum cost chromatic partition problem,' CIAC 1997 (LNCS 1203, pp. 25-36): DP solves vertex chromatic sum on treewidth-k graphs in O(n*(log n)^(k+1)) time; this is FPT-bounded because an optimal sum coloring uses O(tw*log n) colors (Grundy-number bound), giving f(tw)*poly(n).

parameter: number of bins/machines m (natural parameter; not explicitly named in task)
citation: Garey & Johnson, 'Computers and Intractability', W.H. Freeman, 1979, appendix [SP19] MINIMUM SUM OF SQUARES — catalog authority that the general-K problem is NP-complete (a genuine main entry asserting completeness, unlike its NP-membership-open neighbors [SP20]/[SP21]). Problem definition: Chandra & Wong, SIAM J. Comput. 4(3):249-263, 1975 (reference only).
proof_text: PROVEN-HERE (Gate-4, 2026-07-24). Fixed m=2 => para-NP-hard by parameter m, via PARTITION. Given a PARTITION instance S={s_1,...,s_n}, total T=sum s_i, build the MINIMUM-SUM-OF-SQUARES instance with the same sizes and m=2 machines. Any 2-partition with one side summing to x has objective x^2+(T-x)^2, which over x is minimized at x=T/2 with value T^2/2 and is strictly larger for x!=T/2. Hence the instance admits objective <= T^2/2 iff some subset sums to exactly T/2 iff S is a PARTITION yes-instance. PARTITION is NP-complete (Karp 1972; G&J [SP12]); therefore MINIMUM SUM OF SQUARES is NP-hard already at the fixed constant m=2, i.e. para-NP-hard parameterized by m. QED.

parameter: number of inner (interior) points k
citation: M. Hoffmann & Y. Okamoto, 'The minimum weight triangulation problem with few inner points,' IWPEC 2004 (LNCS 3162, pp. 200-212), journal version Comput. Geom. 34(3):149-158, 2006: MWT of a point set with k interior points computable in O(6^k * n^5 * log n) time (improved to 2^{O(sqrt(k) log k)}*poly(n) by Knauer & Spillner, WG 2006, LNCS 4271).

parameter: dimension d (number of weight dimensions / packing constraints)
citation: For d=1 the problem is the classical 0/1 Knapsack, NP-complete (Karp, 'Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems,' 1972; Garey & Johnson 1979, MP9); NP-hardness at the fixed value d=1 yields para-NP-hardness parameterized by d. (Refinement: the unary/pseudo-poly variant, multidimensional subset sum, is W[1]-hard parameterized by the number of dimensions even with unary weights, via a Multicolored-Clique reduction.)

parameter: treewidth (of the variable-clause incidence graph)
citation: SAT (hence 3-SAT, planar 3-SAT, and MAX-SAT) is FPT parameterized by incidence treewidth: Samer & Szeider, 'Algorithms for propositional model counting,' J. Discrete Algorithms 8(1):50-64, 2010 (conf. 2006), time O(4^{tw}*poly); more generally Courcelle's theorem (1990) gives FPT for MSO properties on bounded-treewidth structures.

parameter: reversal distance k (number of reversals)
citation: Jiang, Zhang & Zhu, 'Weak Kernels', ECCC TR10-005 (2010, rev. 2012): Sorting an UNSIGNED permutation by the minimum number of reversals admits a weak kernel of size 4k, giving the first FPT algorithm, running in O(2^{2k} n + n log n) time, parameterized by the reversal distance k.

parameter: number of terminal pairs (equivalently number of terminals |R| = 2 x pairs)
citation: Feldmann & Marx, 'The Complexity Landscape of Fixed-Parameter Directed Steiner Network Problems', ICALP 2016 / ACM Trans. Comput. Theory 15(3-4):1-45 (2023): the partition of terminals into solution trees 'implies the fixed-parameter tractability of Steiner Forest parameterized by k=|R|' (undirected), solving each class via Dreyfus & Wagner (1971) Steiner Tree in 3^{|R|} poly(n).

parameter: natural parameter = height of the (optimal) packing, the minimization objective
citation: Ashok, Kolay, Meesum & Saurabh, 'Parameterized complexity of Strip Packing and Minimum Volume Packing', Theoretical Computer Science 661:56-64 (2017): 2D Strip Packing is W[1]-hard parameterized by the height of the optimal packing (and FPT when parameterized by height plus the maximum item dimension).

parameter: number of machines m
citation: R||Cmax generalizes P2||Cmax (set p_1j=p_2j=p_j); minimizing makespan on 2 identical machines is NP-complete by reduction from PARTITION (Garey & Johnson, 'Computers and Intractability', W.H. Freeman, 1979; classified in Lenstra, Rinnooy Kan & Brucker, 'Complexity of machine scheduling problems', Annals of Discrete Mathematics 1:343-362, 1977). NP-hard at the fixed constant m=2, therefore para-NP-hard parameterized by the number of machines m.

parameter: number of machines m
citation: Minimizing total weighted completion time on 2 identical parallel machines (P2||sum w_j C_j) is NP-hard: Bruno, Coffman & Sethi, 'Scheduling independent tasks to reduce mean finishing time', Communications of the ACM 17(7):382-387, 1974 (also classified in Lenstra, Rinnooy Kan & Brucker, Annals of Discrete Mathematics 1:343-362, 1977). NP-hard at the fixed constant m=2, therefore para-NP-hard parameterized by the number of machines m.
